title: The panel file is split so the dock and its sections are separate work
goal: One file holds the whole right hand panel: how it shares out its height, how it scrolls to what you picked, the layers list, the rows in that list, the measure tool settings, the measurements list, the effects rows and every unit word. It is 5,017 lines and 123 of the last week’s commits touched it. Every feature in the current focus edits it, so every feature waits on it.
notes:
Held back twice on purpose (manager passes 2026-09-04 and 2026-09-08) so capability work went first. It has now grown from about 4,000 lines to 5,017 in one day, and the height-sharing code in it is what three open decision cards are all arguing about, so the next round of panel work will be easier to reason about after this than before it.

Sources/Photonz/LayersPanel.swift, 5,017 lines / 256KB. Seams already marked in the file: InspectorPanel plus its height budget and its three reveal routines (lines 70-1200), the section id enum and drop delegates (1316-1690), CollapsibleSection and the resize handles (1691-2013), the layers list and its rows (2014-2843), the per-tool inspectors (2844-3065), the measurements list (3066-3264), the effects and shadow inspectors (3265 on).

The app already has a precedent for this: "The canvas splits its drawing and its gestures into their own files" landed 2026-09-06, and the CanvasView/CanvasDisplay/CanvasPointerDrags/CanvasMeasure split is the shape to copy. Keep Swift 6 strict concurrency clean and do not introduce a @preconcurrency anywhere.
acceptance: The panel is split along the seams it already has, so no file left behind is over about 1,500 lines, and each new file says in one sentence at the top what it owns

Nothing a person sees changes: Scripts/test.sh passes and the panel walks (panel-start-margin, effects-fit-one-open, dock-picked-first-reveal where it passes today, one-unit-word) pass exactly as they did before the split
The split is a move, not a rewrite: no behaviour is corrected on the way through, and anything found broken is filed rather than fixed here
anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task
